variable_description: The AHECC code for the goods on this export line, which is the column that says what was actually shipped. ABS describes the AHECC as "the product classification used to identify goods being exported from Australia", built as an Australian extension of the World Customs Organization's Harmonized System. The first six digits are the HS subheading and are internationally comparable; the last two are an ABS statistical code and are not. sitc_item_code_ex and anzsic_06_class_code on the same row are both derived from this value, so they add a different arrangement of the same fact rather than new information about the good.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Harmonized Export Commodity Classification (AHECC), 2022
value_definition: An 8-digit AHECC code: HS chapter, heading and subheading in the first six digits, and an ABS statistical code in the last two. The edition in force moves with the Harmonized System revision cycle, most recently AHECC 2022. The full code list is published in the AHECC itself and is not listed here.
limitation: It is not the import classification, and ABS warns that the Working Tariff and the AHECC are not interchangeable, so an export code cannot be matched to commodity_code_im below the shared six-digit HS subheading. It is also unstable as a time series: each Harmonized System revision creates, merges and deletes codes, so a code counted either side of the 2012, 2017 or 2022 changeover need not cover the same goods, and a long run has to be built through the correspondence tables rather than on the code itself.

variable_description: The Customs Tariff code for the goods on this import line, the classification that decides what rate of duty was payable. ABS records that "since 1 January 1988, all goods requiring a full customs declaration for import into Australia are classified according to the ten-digit Harmonized Tariff Item Statistical Code (HTISC) of the Customs Tariff". The first six digits are the HS subheading, the next two complete the Australian tariff item that carries the rate, and the last two are an ABS statistical code. sitc_item_code_im, bec_group_code_im and anzsic_06_class_code are all assigned from this value.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Classifications
value_definition: A 10-digit HTISC from the Combined Australian Customs Tariff Nomenclature and Statistical Classification, the Working Tariff. The edition follows the Harmonized System revision cycle, so which code was valid depends on the reference period of the row. The full item list is published in the Working Tariff and is not listed here.
limitation: The tariff item is a legal classification chosen by the declarant and contestable with Home Affairs, so two importers can enter the same product under different items where the boundary is arguable, and later amendment does not always flow back into the statistics. It also cannot be joined to the export commodity code below the six-digit HS subheading, because the Working Tariff and the AHECC extend the Harmonized System in different directions, and it says nothing about the rate actually paid, which depends on preference_code_im and treatment_code_im.

variable_description: The economic commodity grouping for the exported goods, which ABS derives from the AHECC code on the same row. Revision 4 of the Standard International Trade Classification arranges goods by stage of processing, industrial origin and material, which is why export series are published and compared internationally on this basis rather than on the commodity code. The derivation is mechanical: ABS states that "it is possible to link data (with the exception of refined petroleum products) at the five-digit SITC level to the six-digit level of the HS classification". Its value here is that it aggregates cleanly, which the eight-digit AHECC code does not.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Classifications
value_definition: A five-digit SITC Rev. 4 basic heading, which rolls up to the three-digit group, the two-digit division and the one-digit section. Australian trade statistics have been compiled on a Rev. 4 basis since July 2005. The full basic-heading list is published in SITC Rev. 4 and is not listed here.
limitation: The basic heading does not carry back across that changeover. Moving from Rev. 3 to Rev. 4 deleted 247 basic headings and added 84 new ones, so strict period-to-period comparability was lost for a number of series and a five-digit run spanning July 2005 is not continuous; the two- and three-digit levels survive the break better. The classification is also silent on who bought the goods and why, so it cannot be read as a split between inputs and final demand.

variable_description: The Standard International Trade Classification heading for the imported goods, assigned by ABS from the 10-digit tariff code. It is one of three derived readings of the same import line: this column gives the economic commodity grouping, bec_group_code_im gives the end use, and anzsic_06_class_code gives the industry, so the three answer different questions about one shipment. ABS presents Australian trade "on a SITC (Rev. 4) basis from July 2005 but prior to this the series are on a SITC (Rev. 3) basis", which fixes the edition a reader should assume for BLADE-era records.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Classifications
value_definition: A five-digit SITC Rev. 4 basic heading, aggregable to the three-digit group, two-digit division and one-digit section. It is a derived field: the reported classification on an import line is the HTISC, not this. The full basic-heading list is published in SITC Rev. 4 and is not listed here.
limitation: It carries nothing about duty, because SITC has no relationship to the tariff schedule - preference_code_im, treatment_code_im and commodity_code_im are the columns that do - and many tariff items collapse into one heading, so the mapping cannot be reversed. Refined petroleum products are the documented exception to the link between the five-digit heading and the six-digit Harmonized System subheading, so those commodities should be analysed at the tariff code instead.

variable_description: What the imported goods are mainly for - consumption, capital or intermediate use - on the UN Broad Economic Categories. ABS describes BEC as "a three-digit classification that groups commodities according to their main end use, that is, consumption goods, capital goods and intermediate goods". It is assigned from the tariff code on the same row rather than reported by the importer, so it offers an economic reading of the shipment rather than fresh information about it. This is the column to use when imports have to be split into business inputs and final demand.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Classifications
value_definition: A UN BEC Rev. 4 code, three digits at its most detailed, whose leading digits give the broad category and whose full value gives the end-use detail. It collapses to the consumption, capital and intermediate goods classes used in national accounts work.
limitation: End use here is inferred from the commodity, never observed. A passenger vehicle bought as business equipment and one bought by a household carry the same code, so the split between capital and consumption is a convention applied to the good rather than a measurement of the purchase. The assignment also runs through the Harmonized System, which means a tariff revision that moves a good between codes can move it between end-use categories without anything changing in the trade.

variable_description: Whether the goods on this import line were entered under a preferential rate of duty, and which agreement or scheme was claimed. Home Affairs sets the code when the declaration is lodged, and ABS publishes and extends the list as agreements enter force - it added "Preference code AE, for the Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)" in December 2025. The code qualifies the duty treatment of the line rather than describing the goods, so it is the closest thing in this table to a free trade agreement marker.

value_definition: A short Home Affairs preference code, mostly one or two letters, empty or a no-preference value where the goods entered at the general rate. The list is open-ended and grows as new trade agreements commence.
limitation: The code is a claim made on the declaration, not evidence that duty was forgone or that the origin rules were met. It names the scheme claimed under, so it is not a country of origin - country_of_origin_im carries that - and a line can be preference-coded and still attract duty. Because codes are added as agreements commence, a rise in preferential lines can be an artefact of the code list growing rather than a change in trading behaviour.

variable_description: Whether the import line was entered under a concession or other special customs treatment, usually one that reduces or removes duty. ABS notes that it "receives a range of information about the customs procedures applied to transactions" and that "this includes the line nature type, treatment code, duty fields and GST fields", so this column is one of a set describing how the line was processed rather than what was in it. The codes attach to the concessional items in Schedule 4 of the Customs Tariff, and ABS extends the published list as new concessions are legislated - treatment code 141 for petroleum-based oils eligible for a refund of duty was added in July 2024. A value of '000' means no treatment code, which is the ordinary case.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018, Data sources and compilation methods
value_definition: A three-digit Department of Home Affairs treatment code, with '000' standing for no treatment. The list is open and grows over time as concessional items are added to Schedule 4.
limitation: The code describes the duty treatment, not the goods, so it cannot stand in for what was imported and it cannot be aggregated with the commodity classifications. It also gives no money: the duty forgone under a concession depends on the general rate and the customs value, and neither is recoverable from this column. Because a code exists only from the date its concession was legislated, a series built on one code shows a concession appearing when it was coded rather than when the trade started.

value_domain: ABS nature of tariff code (single letter)
values: C: Confidential - This is set when ABS confidentialises data.
G: Government - Includes imports for Government.
N: Normal - Items attracting the rate of duty as prescribed in Schedule 3 of the Customs Tariff.
Q: Quota - This covers goods entered under the quota provisions of the Customs Tariff.
R: Concessional - Includes goods where a concessional rate of duty applies.
value_source: ABS, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018 (cat. 5489.0), Data downloads workbook 5489_2026.xlsx, Appendix 10 section A 'Nature of tariff'
rationale: Appendix 10 section A gives the complete 5-code list with labels and descriptions. It is an ABS-created data item, not a Home Affairs one, which is why it is documented in the ABS CSM rather than in the Customs Tariff.
evidence_quote: N | Normal | Items attracting the rate of duty as prescribed in Schedule 3
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review recorded no codeframe; the appendix the Data Item List cites contains it in full.
variable_description: A single letter recording the kind of tariff arrangement the import line was dutied under - duty information rather than information about the goods. It is the third of three duty qualifiers on the row: preference_code_im names the agreement claimed, treatment_code_im names the concession applied, and this records the nature of the tariff in play when the duty was worked out. ABS publishes the code list in the appendices to its merchandise trade concepts, sources and methods, beside the treatment and preference code lists.
description_source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, International Merchandise Trade, Australia: Concepts, Sources and Methods, 2018 (cat. 5489.0), appendices
value_definition: A single alphabetic character from an ABS code list published with the merchandise trade appendices. The domain is small and closed, and it is unrelated to the numeric preference and treatment code lists on the same row.
limitation: It is not the nature of the entry. Nature 10, 20 and 30 - direct home consumption, warehousing, and clearance from a bonded warehouse - are the line nature type, and form_id_im carries them, so reading this column as the declaration type puts warehoused goods in the wrong bucket. Nor does it give an amount: no duty rate, duty paid or concession value can be recovered from a letter, and the customs value on the line is unaffected by it.

value_domain: IP classification symbol; the system depends on classification_system and ip_right_type - IPC or CPC symbol (patents), Nice class number (trade marks), Australian Locarno-based design class (designs), UPOV code or genus / genus-species name (plant breeder's rights)
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, Table 8 application-classification; values read from the published IP RAPID application_classification.csv
rationale: The column holds the classification symbol itself, drawn from whichever system the sibling classification_type names (IPC and CPC for patents, Nice for trade marks, Locarno for designs, UPOV and botanical names for plant breeder's rights). The sample keeps the bare symbols: a 'system: symbol' rendering would be read as code-and-label and emit the system name into the column.
evidence_quote: IPC mark (patents), Nice (trade marks), Locarno (designs), UPOV (PBR)
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review had no Appendix 15. IP Australia publishes the equivalent as the IP RAPID data dictionary, and the underlying data is open, so both the definition and real values are available.
variable_description: The classification symbol recorded against one IP right, at the depth the relevant examining area uses. Which scheme the symbol belongs to is set by classification_system and ip_right_type on the same row: an IPC or CPC symbol for a patent, a Nice class number for a trade mark, an Australian Locarno-based class for a design, and a UPOV code or genus name for a plant breeder's right. classification_date and classification_removal_date bound the period the symbol applied, and c_is_current marks the symbols in force at the extract. classification_area holds the simplified reading of the same value.
description_source: IP Australia, Open IP data (IP RAPID), and the IPGOD table documentation published through the Australian Research Data Commons
value_definition: A string whose shape follows the scheme it comes from, with no single fixed width: an IPC or CPC symbol such as A61K 31/00 for patents, a one- or two-digit Nice class number for trade marks, a Locarno-based class number for designs, and a UPOV code or a genus or genus-species name for plant breeder's rights. The full symbol list is published by WIPO and IP Australia and is not listed here.
limitation: A symbol records where an examiner filed the document so that it can be searched, not what the right legally covers, and the two diverge: a patent claim can run well beyond the technology its symbol names. Reclassification rewrites the value as schemes are revised, so the symbol on the row is the one that applies now rather than the one assigned at filing. A patent carried in both IPC and CPC also appears twice with different symbols, so counting distinct values here counts schemes as well as subjects.

value_domain: Simplified classification area: WIPO technology field (patents), Nice class symbol (trade marks), first two digits of the Locarno class (designs), plant group (plant breeder's rights)
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, Table 8 application-classification; distinct values read from the published IP RAPID application_classification.csv
rationale: The BLADE description is the IP RAPID dictionary's wording verbatim. All 100 distinct values were tallied over the full published extract. Patents give the 35 WIPO technology-concordance fields as '<number>_<field name>' plus 99_unknown (concordance itself published by WIPO at https://www.wipo.int/documents/2948119/3215563/wipo_ipc_technology.pdf); trade marks give a bare Nice class number 1-45; designs give a two-digit Locarno class, zero-padded, so '01'-'09' are unambiguously designs while '10'-'32' are shared with Nice; PBR gives eight plant groups (ornamentals, fruit_crops, field_crops_(cereals), field_crops_(non-cereals), vegetable_crops, forage_crops, amenity_grasses_and_turf, fungi). An empty string occurs on 95,732 rows. The companion coarse_classification_area takes 10 values.
evidence_quote: Classification area provides a simplification of the IP right system
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review had no Appendix 16. The IP RAPID dictionary defines the field and the open data gives the full observed domain.
variable_description: A simplified subject area for the IP right, set so that patents, trade marks, designs and plant breeder's rights can be counted side by side. It is a roll-up of the classification symbol on the same row, and what the label means depends on ip_right_type: a WIPO technology field for a patent, a Nice class for a trade mark, the first two digits of the Locarno class for a design, and a plant group for a plant breeder's right. coarse_classification_area aggregates it further, and classification_system names the scheme the underlying symbol came from. It is the column to reach for when a portfolio has to be described across all four IP RAPID right types at once.
description_source: IP Australia, Open IP data (IP RAPID), and the IPGOD table documentation published through the Australian Research Data Commons
value_definition: A short text label rather than a numeric code, drawn from a different label set for each right type: WIPO technology fields for patents, Nice classes for trade marks, two-digit Locarno-based areas for designs, and plant groups for plant breeder's rights.
limitation: The areas are not comparable between right types. A patent's technology field describes what an invention does; a trade mark's Nice class describes what a mark is registered for, so adding chemistry patents to chemicals trade marks does not make one series. The column also cannot be summed straight to an application count, because an application carrying several classifications contributes several rows, and it says nothing about how commercially significant the area is to the applicant.

value_domain: IP Australia party role (role of a party on an IP right)
value_source: IP Australia, IP RAPID Data Dictionary, Table 11 'Party role definitions & categories by right type'; distinct values read from the published IP RAPID party_activity.csv
rationale: BLADE table 34 is the IP RAPID Party table and the BLADE description, including the note that a party can hold several roles concurrently, is the IP RAPID dictionary's wording verbatim. The 51 values listed are every distinct party_role in the published extract (12,397,185 rows), ordered by frequency: agent 4,251,049, applicant 4,154,490, owner 2,261,549, patentee 789,750. The dictionary's Table 11 documents 49 roles by right type; it omits four that occur in the data (agent_for_opposition, applicant_being_opposed, breeder, qualified_person) and lists two that do not (designer, thd_pty_inq). Roles roll up to nine party_role_category values: applicant, applicant_agent, opposition, opposition_agent, other, other_agent, non_use_applicant, mortgagee, licensee.
evidence_quote: The role of the party associated with this IP right
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review had no Appendix 20. IP Australia's IP RAPID dictionary is the appendix's public equivalent, and the open data confirms the domain.
variable_description: What a person or business was to this IP right - applicant, owner, inventor, agent or the equivalent - over the period the row covers. A row is a party, a role and a period rather than a party, because one party can hold several roles at once and one right can have several parties in the same role, which makes the table many-to-many in both directions. effective_from_date and effective_to_date bound the period, p_is_current marks the role held at the extract and is_founding marks the earliest party in that role, while party_role_category groups the roles into broader classes.
description_source: IP Australia, Open IP data (IP RAPID), and the IPGOD table documentation published through the Australian Research Data Commons
value_definition: A short text role label taken from a role list that differs by right type, covering applicant, owner, inventor and agent roles for patents, trade marks and designs, and breeder-side roles for plant breeder's rights. party_role_category carries the coarser grouping of the same value.
limitation: The label does not tell you who benefits from the right. Attorneys and address-for-service parties sit in this table beside owners, so joining businesses to IP rights without filtering the role attributes a patent to the firm that filed it as well as to the firm that holds it. Nor does the role alone establish ownership at a date: an assignment closes one role period and opens another, so ownership at a point in time has to be read from the effective date columns, and a party that is both applicant and owner will appear more than once for the same right.
